target.title: fix(gateway): cancel unread cron webhook bodies before SSRF release
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron webhook delivery (`postCronWebhook`) posts via `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, then
calls `release()` without reading status or body. `release()` tears down the
SSRF dispatcher but does **not** cancel an unread response body. Under undici,
that leaves the TCP connection pinned until the webhook server finishes (or
forever on a stalled/large body), so each fire-and-forget cron webhook can
retain a socket in the long-lived gateway process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cancel the unread body in `postCronWebhook` before `release()` when
`!response.bodyUsed`. Delivery semantics stay the same: webhooks remain
best-effort fire-and-forget (no status checks); cancel failures are swallowed so
they cannot mask fetch/SSRF errors.

## User Impact

**Before:** A cron webhook endpoint that streams or holds its response body
could leave the request socket open after gateway notification dispatch
returned.

**After:** The production webhook path cancels the unread body and the server
observes prompt socket close, without changing webhook payload, timeout, or
SSRF policy.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.ts`,
  `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.test.ts`,
  `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.transport.test.ts`,
  `src/gateway/server-cron.test.ts`
- Production path: `sendGatewayCronFailureAlert` /
  `dispatchGatewayCronFinishedNotifications` → `postCronWebhook` →
  `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → cancel unread body → `release()`
- Compatibility: webhook timeout (10s), payload shape, and production SSRF
  policy (no private-network allow) unchanged

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Fire-and-forget cron webhooks must cancel unread response bodies so undici
releases the TCP socket promptly. Without cancel, a streaming 200 body that
never ends keeps `serverObservedSocketClose: false` 250ms after
`sendGatewayCronFailureAlert` returns.

### Canonical reachability path

`sendGatewayCronFailureAlert({ mode: "webhook" })` → `postCronWebhook` →
`fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `!response.bodyUsed` → `response.body.cancel()` →
`release()`

(Same helper is used by completion and failure-destination webhook fanout.)

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses existing `fetchWithSsrFGuard`. No new config, timeout, or webhook URL
surface. Matches sibling cancel-before-release cleanup (cron model preflight /
thread-ownership / browser CDP).

### Real environment tested

**Real Node HTTP + real `fetchWithSsrFGuard` (production `sendGatewayCronFailureAlert`):**

- Loopback `node:http` server writes headers + partial `{"accepted":` and never
  ends the body
- Transport harness only adds `allowPrivateNetwork: true` so loopback is
  reachable; production `postCronWebhook` still omits that policy
- Calls production `sendGatewayCronFailureAlert` with `mode: "webhook"`
- Observes server-side TCP `socket` `close` promptly after return
- macOS, Node v22.23.1

Negative control (same harness, cancel removed):

```text
{"productionFunction":"sendGatewayCronFailureAlert","returnedAtMs":250,"serverObservedSocketClose":false,"socketCloseAfterStartMs":null}
```

After fix:

```text
{"productionFunction":"sendGatewayCronFailureAlert","returnedAtMs":0,"serverObservedSocketClose":true,"socketCloseAfterStartMs":0}
```

Webhook dispatch still completes in both runs; only socket release changes.

### Evidence after fix

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.transport.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose

 ✓ |gateway-server| …/server-cron-notifications.transport.test.ts > postCronWebhook transport body cleanup > cancels unread failure-alert webhook bodies and closes the request socket
 ✓ |gateway-server| …/server-cron-notifications.test.ts > … (11)

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  12 passed (12)
```

```text
./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check \
  src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.ts \
  src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.transport.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-cron.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.
```

Premise: Undici requires every response body to be consumed or canceled; GC does
not promptly release connection resources. Cron webhooks never read the body.

AI-assisted: Yes.
